new_statements.quote: 2.4 WORDS AND STRESS. Morphemes may be classed as bound affixes,12) partially free clitics, and free words. Words are stressed, and clitics are unstressed unless they occur at the center of an intonation contour. 2.41 WORDS. Words, both derived and non-derived, are stressed on the final syllable. This word stress, however, is very slight, and it is often skewed by the position of the word in the intonation contour. The word stress is not contrastive.13) [anjaú] /anjaw/ 'to visit' [diŋanjauí] /dianjawi/ 'to be visited'. [fn. 13, p. 48:] However, a few non-Lampung place names have a penultimate stress, for example: [palémbaŋ] 'Palembang', [jakárta] 'Jakarta', [indonésya] 'Indonesia'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable of the word, including derived (suffixed) words, where it moves to the new final syllable (anjaw -> di-anjaw-i stressed on -i). Stress is weak, non-contrastive, and can be overridden by phrase intonation. Clitics (proclitics and enclitics such as possessive mu, ku, emphatic lah) are unstressed and outside the stress domain ([lambánmo] /lamban mu/), except that the last clitic of a clitic series takes stress when no free word follows in the same contour.
new_statements.exceptions: A few non-Lampung place names (loans) have penultimate stress: Palembang, Jakarta, Indonesia (fn. 13). Clitics unstressed; last clitic in a series stressed if not followed by a free word in the same intonation contour (p. 6).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the word including derivational/inflectional suffixes but excluding enclitics; author notes word stress is 'very slight' and often skewed by position in the intonation contour (phrase-level intonation treated separately in 2.5 with three terminals and two pitch levels).
new_statements.identity_note: sout3224 'Southern Pesisir' [pec] is a Glottolog Bookkeeping entry for a retired Ethnologue code merged (ISO CR 2007-142, 2008) into Lampung Api [ljp] = Glottolog lamp1243. Walker 1976 describes the Way Lima dialect, which he places (sec. 1.2, p. 1) in the 'southern' Pesisir grouping together with Kota Agung, Kalianda and Telukbetung, i.e. exactly the old [pec] Southern Pesisir; his other informants were from Kota Agung and Telukbetung. The statement therefore applies first-hand to this variety and, by extension, is the primary stress description usually cited for Lampung Api (lamp1243) as a whole. Note a parallel session holds the same NUSA 2 scan under (Sungkai, another retired Lampung Api code).

sources.note: Sec. 2.4-2.41 p. 5: words (derived and non-derived) are stressed on the final syllable; stress very slight, often skewed by position in the intonation contour, not contrastive; clitics unstressed unless at the centre of an intonation contour (2.42; p. 6: in a clitic series not followed by a free word the last clitic is stressed; examples [lambánmo] /lamban mu/ 'your house' show enclitics outside the stress domain). Fn. 13 p. 48: a few non-Lampung place names have penultimate stress ([palémbaŋ], [jakárta], [indonésya]).
